correctness.rationale: Any compact connected finite-length competitor meeting all four equal disks may be replaced by a Steiner minimum tree on selected contact points, no greater in length. For four terminals, three paired two-junction trees plus allowed degenerations exhaust Steiner topologies. Eliminating disk contacts gives convex costs ||u-v||+sum_i (||u-c_i||-r)_+. Symmetry averaging for adjacent pairings yields u=(-t,0),v=(t,0); differentiating 2t+4(max(sqrt((a-t)^2+a^2)-r,0)) gives t*=a(1-1/sqrt3), critical r=2a/sqrt3, then clipped segment t_r=a-sqrt(r²-a²). Opposite-corner pairing has optimal u=v=0 and value 4(max(sqrt2*a-r,0)); strict derivative comparison shows it never wins before collapse. Explicit trees and singleton attain all boundary regimes. Independently checked analytic branches against 3-topology scipy optimization for multiple radii; finite numerical comparison corroborates rather than replaces exhaustive topological/convex argument.
residual_risks: Classical four-terminal Steiner topology completeness is invoked rather than reproved from first principles; the proof does not characterize uniqueness of all critical minimizers.
